messages.subject: Queryable Database Demo Failing
parts:
I am running on a single instance hadoop pseudo-cluster. I decided to
only load one single airline file (the 1990 one). I was not able to
get the distributed version to download (probably due to proxy or
something). Anyway, I was able to convert the file to R objects with
your demo code.

Now, I am trying to run the Queryable Database demo, and I get this
error:

R ERROR BEGIN (map):
=============

Error in split.default(seq_len(nrow(x)), f, drop = drop, ...) :
Group length is 0 but data length > 0


Is this possibly due to only having one year of data, or what would
you suggest looking at?

Thanks from this noob! :-)
-M@

map <- expression({
h <- do.call("rbind",map.values)
d <- h[h$carrier=='WN',,drop=FALSE]

e <- split(d,list(d$year,d$month,d$mday))
lapply(e,function(r){
k <- as.vector(unlist(r[1,c("year","month","mday")])) ## remove

reduce <- expression(
pre = { collec <- NULL },
reduce = {

messages.subject: Re: [rhipe] Re: Queryable Database Demo Failing
parts:
Hi,

So your error is

Error in split.default(seq_len(nrow(x)), f, drop = drop, ...) :
> > Group length is 0 but data length > 0

but mine is something to do with a vector. Anyways, it appears the
split function in the map might be causing it.

So, remove the reduce (we don't need it - the data wont get to the reduce, the
job will fail before it can).

And rewrite the map to look like

map <- expression({
h <- do.call("rbind",map.values)
d <- h[h$carrier=='WN',,drop=FALSE]

if(nrow(d)>0){
e <- split(d,list(d$year,d$month,d$mday))
lapply(e,function(r){
k <- as.vector(unlist(r[1,c("year","month","mday")])) ##
remove attributes
rhcollect(k, r)
})
}

},error=function(er) {
rhcounter("err",er,1)
rhcollect("error",list(er,d))
}
)
})

Notice that this block

if(nrow(d)>0){
e <- split(d,list(d$year,d$month,d$mday))
lapply(e,function(r){
k <- as.vector(unlist(r[1,c("year","month","mday")])) ##
remove attributes
rhcollect(k, r)
})
}

is wrapped in tryCatch and if an error happens the we catch it in the 'error'
parameter. Instead of failing the job, we write the error message and the data
'd'. (It could be possible to fail the job - you could save the offending
objects to a unique filename on the HDFS).

Now lets read one error (btw, it is possible that not all key-values correspond
to errors, if errors are few you might want another mapreduce on the output to
subset error kv pairs or dont even use rhcollect(k,r) (in above code)).

x <- rhread("/tmp/southwest",type='map',max=1)
h <- x[[1]][[2]][[2]]

Now stepping through the above code, the line

e <- split(d,list(d$year,d$month,d$mday))

is the offender and that's because d does not have the column mday (my
typo). So replace mday with 'day' (everywhere) and try again.

What version of R are you using? My error was different, but i guess it's the
same cause.


Cheers
Joy

rhgetkey should work, so try

your output path

should return a k-v pair.

Saptarshi
